content:
Last week, Bloomberg reported that Apple is developing a screenless fitness band, similar to WHOOP or Fitbit Air. As someone who has been using WHOOP for the past six months, I do think the concept is solid, but there are a few things I hope Apple can do better.

Since the product is still in early development, we don't have many details about Apple's screenless fitness band for now. It won't be released until at the earliest 2028. Bloomberg described it as "a slim fabric strap with a built-in sensor and computing module."

Earlier this year, WHOOP partnered with Chase on a promotion where you could get a WHOOP at a discount or for free with a Chase Sapphire card, so I took advantage of it. I've been using WHOOP ever since, though I never fully committed to using it.

The reason is simple: automatic workout detection will never be perfect. I found that I had to specifically pull out my phone to log workouts both before and after exercising, which is really annoying. With Apple Watch, you can start logging a workout directly on the screen, and WHOOP will sync the timing from Apple Health. That's the main reason I keep wearing my Apple Watch.

Going to the gym is tolerable for pulling out my phone, but for more casual activities like cycling or walking, I don't want to bother with my phone.

So, for Apple's screenless fitness band, I'd love to see physical buttons and indicator lights that can be used to start and stop workout logging. You'd still need to categorize the workout on your phone afterwards, but I'd rather deal with that later than fiddle around during the workout. Apple could also develop a classification model based on certain factors.

Summary

If Apple can really develop a screenless fitness band that's convenient to use without constantly pulling out your phone, I think it would be very appealing. This form factor has many advantages, including being more comfortable to wear, longer battery life, and being able to be worn alongside a traditional watch.

The most upvoted comment was posted by TB

I bought the FitBit Air because I'm kind of tired of wearing my Apple Watch. I like wearing mechanical watches, but I still want to monitor my health data and enjoy the convenience of a smartwatch without constantly pulling out my phone (i.e., quick access to Apple Pay, unlocking doors with tired hands, etc.). If Apple can come out with a product that fully integrates into the ecosystem, lets me use a simplified Apple Pay, door keys, car keys, and other NFC features, and can connect to my AirPods to have Siri read notifications or perform actions for me, I'd be first in line to buy it.

Personally, after evaluating WHOOP, I found I prefer wearing a smartwatch directly, even though the battery life is worse. I understand some people prefer a screenless one to avoid distractions, but I personally just turn on Do Not Disturb mode on my watch.

What do you think about Apple developing a screenless fitness band? What price point would make you willing to buy one? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
